title: Meta Reports Muse Hits 10M Users, Shopping Emerges as Top Activity, TechCrunch Reveals
body:
Meta Platforms announced on Wednesday that its AI‑driven personal assistant, Muse, has surpassed the 10‑million‑user milestone, underscoring the app’s rapid adoption for both shopping and productivity tasks. The figure was disclosed during the company’s third‑quarter earnings call, where executives highlighted Muse’s role in expanding Meta’s services beyond its core social‑media ecosystem and positioning the firm to capture a larger slice of the burgeoning AI‑assisted commerce market.

The milestone arrives at a time when Meta is aggressively diversifying its revenue streams. While advertising still accounts for the bulk of the company’s earnings, the firm has been investing heavily in artificial‑intelligence products that can generate new monetisation avenues. Muse, which integrates generative‑AI chat capabilities with Meta’s extensive data on user preferences, is being positioned as a “shopping companion” that can recommend products, compare prices and even complete purchases within the app. According to Meta’s CFO, a sizable share of active users engage with Muse primarily for retail‑related queries, signaling a shift in how consumers interact with AI tools for everyday transactions.

Industry analysts see the 10‑million‑user count as a validation of Meta’s broader AI strategy, but they caution that the metric alone does not guarantee profitability. “User growth is encouraging, yet the key will be converting those interactions into measurable commerce revenue,” said Priya Desai, a senior analyst at GlobalTech Insights. She noted that competitors such as Amazon’s Alexa and Google’s Gemini are also courting the same user base, each leveraging their own ecosystems to embed shopping experiences. Meta’s advantage lies in its massive social graph, which can feed Muse with contextual insights about a user’s tastes, friends’ recommendations and trending products, potentially delivering more personalised suggestions than rivals.

From a financial perspective, Meta’s Q3 earnings reflected modest top‑line growth, with advertising revenue holding steady despite a competitive ad market. The company attributed part of its resilience to “new AI‑driven experiences” that keep users engaged longer on its platforms. Muse’s integration with Instagram and Facebook—allowing users to summon the assistant while browsing feeds—has reportedly boosted session times and opened pathways for native ad placements within the AI chat flow. However, Meta also disclosed that the app is still in a “growth phase,” with ongoing investments in server capacity and model refinement expected to weigh on operating expenses in the near term.

The broader tech landscape suggests that AI‑enabled shopping could become a pivotal battleground for user attention and spend. Recent surveys indicate that a majority of millennials and Gen‑Z consumers prefer conversational interfaces for product discovery, valuing speed and convenience over traditional search. Muse’s ability to combine visual product recognition—leveraging Meta’s image‑processing tools—with natural‑language dialogue aligns well with these preferences. Moreover, the app’s “personal productivity” features, such as calendar management and task summarisation, aim to make Muse a multi‑purpose digital assistant, increasing the likelihood of daily usage and, by extension, ad exposure.

Looking ahead, Meta plans to roll out additional functionalities for Muse, including deeper integration with its upcoming virtual‑reality platform and the ability to handle more complex transactions, such as subscription services and ticket purchases. Executives hinted that the company is exploring revenue‑sharing models with merchants, which could transform Muse from a user‑acquisition metric into a direct profit centre. As AI continues to blur the lines between social interaction, commerce and productivity, Muse’s growth trajectory will be a key indicator of Meta’s success in redefining its business beyond advertising. The next earnings season will reveal whether the app can translate its expanding user base into sustainable financial performance, shaping the future of AI‑centric commerce across Meta’s ecosystem.
